newsitem.title: USA: Few customers affected by U.S. gas pipeline break.
newsitem.headline: Few customers affected by U.S. gas pipeline break.

text.p: Several industrial customers lost natural gas service after two pipeline explosions in Washington state over the weekend, but residential and general business users were unaffected, officials said Monday.

Repairs were expected to be completed Monday or Tuesday on the 26-inch pipe operated by Northwest Pipeline Corp, which broke in apparently unrelated incidents 220 miles apart Saturday and Sunday, a state engineer said.

He said only 10 feet of pipe needed to be replaced to repair the second break near the town of Kalama, which occurred Sunday and sent up a huge fireball visible in Portland, about 30 miles (50 km) to the south.

A spokesman for Northwest Natural Gas Co said five large industrial customers, mostly paper mills, lost service after the explosion near Kalama. All have backup fuel supplies and contracts allowing their service to be interrupted.
Because Northwest Pipeline operates a parallel 30-inch pipe, none of the 430,000 residential and business customers in the metropolitan Portland area were affected.
A spokesman for Washington Energy Co said none of the company's customers were affected, while a spokesman for Cascade Natural Gas Corp said no residential or commercial customers were affected.
He could not confirm whether service had been interrupted to any large industrial who have backup fuel supplies.
